data.summary: Call an HTTP endpoint and route by node success or node error.

requiredFields.note: Endpoint to call, a string or null (not set). Templates like {{$memory.x}} are interpolated first; a null, empty, blank or non-URL result fails the node before any request.
'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH' or 'DELETE', uppercase. Required: the contract schema rejects any other value or spelling. The engine passes it to the request as is.

optionalFields.note: Credentials: 'basic' (username + password) or 'bearer' (token), read only when enabled is truthy. Omit it for a public endpoint; an API key goes in a header.
Query parameters, one row each. Absent means none ([]). A row is sent only when enabled is truthy and its key is non-empty.
One query parameter: key, value, enabled, description, and an optional row id and type.

Parameter name, interpolated. A row with a missing or empty key is skipped, even when enabled. (when: The parameter entry is skipped when the key is missing or empty, an extra guard headers do not have.)
Parameter value, interpolated: templates like {{$memory.x}} resolve at request time.
Set true or the row is dropped: absent counts as off. (when: The parameter entry is skipped unless this is truthy.)
Free-text note for the row. No HTTP reader of this key is traced in workflow-core.
Optional row id. No effect on execution.
Optional row kind, 'text' or 'file'. No effect on execution.
Request payload: type, content, enabled. Nothing is sent unless enabled is truthy.

Content type. 'application/json', 'multipart/form-data' and 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' each have their own handling; any other value takes the 'application/xml' path. (when: Read only when body.enabled is truthy.)
Set true to send the body: absent or false drops it and the request still goes out.

Open value, kept as written. For JSON, a string, interpolated then parsed at request time. For form and multipart, rows { key, value, enabled }: a row not enabled is dropped. (when: Read only when body.enabled is truthy.)
Request headers, one row each. Absent means none ([]). A row is sent only when enabled is truthy.
One header: key, value, enabled, description, and an optional row id and type.
Header name, interpolated. Unlike a parameter row, a header row with no key is not skipped.
Header value, interpolated. An API key goes here as {{$secret.NAME}} (a key such as X-Api-Key): authentication has no api-key mode.
Set true or the row is dropped: absent counts as off. (when: The header entry is skipped entirely unless this is truthy.)
Free-text note for the row. No HTTP reader of this key is traced in workflow-core.
Optional row id. No effect on execution.
Optional legacy row kind, 'text' or 'file'. No effect on execution.
Transport settings: timeout, TLS, retries, proxy, mTLS. Absent means {}, and each setting falls back to its own default.
Request timeout in ms. No default of its own: the company plan's limit caps an unset, 0 or over-limit value. With mTLS enabled, mtlsTimeout applies instead.
Boolean. Absent means false. What it toggles on the TLS connection is not traced in workflow-core.
Automatic retries. Off unless enabled is truthy: absent or disabled, nothing retries and none of the retry defaults apply.
Outbound proxy, optional. Read only when enabled is truthy, and then auth is read with no guard: an enabled proxy without auth throws while the request is built.
Client certificate (mTLS). Used only with enabled true, an id, and the mTLS service available; otherwise a plain HTTPS agent. A failure building it fails the node before the request.
Timeout in ms while mTLS is on. Absent or non-finite means 30000; clamped to 1000-120000 and never capped by the plan. Not used without mTLS.
Legacy retry count, a non-negative integer. No effect on execution: retries come from settings.retryOptions.retries.
Root-level proxy. Kept as written and never read: the proxy the engine uses is settings.proxyOptions.
Name the response is stored under; absent means 'response'. A CODE node reads it with $context.getHttpResponse('<output>').
Data-loss-prevention settings. No HTTP reader of them is traced in workflow-core.
JavaScript run before the request, as a string. workflow-core never runs it. (when: Executed only when the engine's script feature flag is on.)
JavaScript run after the request, as a string. workflow-core never runs it. (when: Executed only when the engine's script feature flag is on.)
Optional description of the request. No effect on execution.
Optional id of the HTTP tool this request was created from. No effect on execution.
Absent means false. true answers messages the user sends while the call runs with blockedMessage, instead of starting a parallel flow.
Text sent while isBlockingEnabled holds the user. Empty: those messages are dropped silently.
true marks a Datum preset request; the engine then skips the plan's per-request timeout cap. Absent means false.
Datum preset: the chosen database's id. No effect on execution: url and headers hold the request.
Datum preset: the chosen database's slug. No effect on execution: url and headers hold the request.
Datum preset: the chosen database's name. No effect on execution.
Datum preset: the chosen database's base URL. No effect on execution: url holds the request.
Datum preset: the collection name. No effect on execution: url holds it.
Datum preset: the operation, '' until chosen (list_records, list_records_extended, get_record, create_record, update_record, delete_record). No effect on execution: url, method and body hold it.
Datum preset: the record id for get, update and delete, often a template. No effect on execution: url holds it.
Datum preset: field rows for create and update, [{ id, key, value, enabled }]. No effect on execution: body.content holds them.
One field row.
Row id.
Field name.
Field value.
Whether the row is on.
Datum preset: the filter string built from the filter terms. No effect on execution: parameters hold it.
Datum preset: the sort string built from the sort terms. No effect on execution: parameters hold it.
Datum preset: filter rows, [{ id, field, operator, value }]. No effect on execution: datumV2Filter and parameters hold them.
One filter row.
Row id.
Field the row filters on.
Comparison operator, a string.
Value compared against.
Datum preset: sort rows, [{ id, field, direction }]. No effect on execution: datumV2Sort and parameters hold them.
One sort row.
Row id.
Field the row sorts on.
'asc' or 'desc'.
Datum preset: page number for list operations, a positive integer. No effect on execution: parameters hold it.
Datum preset: page size for list operations, a positive integer. No effect on execution: parameters hold it.
Datum preset: snapshot of the collection's fields, [{ name, type, required?, options? }]. No effect on execution.
One field of the collection.
Field name.
Field type, a string.
Optional: whether the field is required.
Optional allowed values.
One allowed value.
The name the author gives the node, e.g. 'Preguntar datos al usuario'. Every node type accepts it. A label only. No effect on execution.
Per-node non-happy-path handlers. Absent: the workspace handlers apply. Present, even empty: they replace the workspace handlers for this node.
Handler the engine runs when this node fails with no edge to follow. The only entry it looks up on non-conditional nodes.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler the engine looks up when a CONDITIONAL node fails with no edge to follow.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler for the exit event. Accepted; the engine does not look it up on a node today.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler for the expire event. Accepted; the engine does not look it up on a node today.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Handler for the invalid_input event. Accepted; the engine does not look it up on a node today.
What the engine does on this event: 'message' sends message, 'skill-redirect' moves to targetSkillId, 'canvas' sends nothing and follows only the node's own edges.
Text sent to the user in 'message' mode, up to 1024 characters. Needed, non-blank, in that mode.
Skill the conversation moves to in 'skill-redirect' mode. Needed in that mode.
Completeness flag stored with the node, false on a new node. Its meaning differs between node types. No effect on execution.
Tracking events emitted after the node runs, at most 10. Each fires when enabled is true and emitOn matches the outcome.
One tracking event: its name, when it fires, an on/off switch and the payload fields.
Event name, recorded as the track name. Up to 255 characters.
false keeps the event configured but never emits it.
When the event fires: 'always' (default when absent), 'success' on a successful run, 'error' on a failed one.
Fields added to the event, each resolved from memory and context when it fires.
One payload field of a tracking event.
Row id of the payload field. No effect on execution.
Key of the value in the event payload. An entry with an empty field is skipped.
Template resolved when the event fires, e.g. '{{$memory.orderId}}'. $env and $secret are not available; a resolution error stores ''.
Optional event id. No effect on whether the event fires.
Optional event kind; 'track' is the only value. No effect on execution.
Optional provenance, 'user' or 'ai'. Copied into the track record when present.
Optional creation timestamp. No effect on execution.
Optional last-update timestamp. No effect on execution.
Copy of the node's collapsed display state. No effect on execution.
Copy of the node's free-text comments. No effect on execution.
Copy of the id of a workflow the node was stored in. The node belongs to the workflow that stores it. No effect on execution.

outletDocs.description: The node succeeded: the response is stored under output and the flow continues. Which HTTP statuses count as success is not traced in workflow-core.
outletDocs.fires: When the request completes without a node error. Every edge wired to it fires, in stored order; none wired ends the run cleanly.

branches.when: Optional: an HTTP node may be the last one. The engine routes it by edge type; write the branch as 'success'.

outletDocs.description: The node failed (an empty or non-URL url, an mTLS setup failure, or a request error). The error follows the failed edge instead of crashing the run.
outletDocs.fires: When the node returns an error. Every failed edge fires, in stored order. None wired: nonHappyPathHandlers.error answers if set, else the workspace error handler.

branches.when: Optional. Never wire it to END: a non-empty failed branch disables both error-handler fallbacks and swallows the error.

notes: body.type 'raw', retryCondition 'network', retryDelay 'fixed' are invalid — the bundled lint checks membership in the three enums and hard-fails.

Never write a literal credential: use {{$secret.NAME}} for an org-level secret (created with `jelou secret set NAME`) or {{$memory.x}} for a value bound by an upstream node. No validator rule catches a literal today, so this is on the author.

pre/postRequestScript run only when the company has the ConfigCat flag brain_experimental_pre_post_request_api_soap_node enabled; the check is fail-closed, so with the flag off the scripts are skipped with no error and the node still reports success.

The script body is wrapped in an async function (await is legal) and runs under a 2 s VM timeout. Globals: $memory (v2 surface, so getJson/setJson work), $context, $input, $output, $env, $secret, $user, $bot, $company, $message, $webhook, and $utils.{dayjs, _, shortly, uuid, crypto, logger}. console/fetch/require/import are absent.
Prefer pre/postRequestScript over single-purpose CODE nodes; inline scripts have no error edge — failures bubble through 'failed'.

Wire 'failed' only for recovery logic (retry, alternate path, persistence, human handoff); for a message-only error reply set nonHappyPathHandlers.error or rely on the project-level default error message — and never wire failed -> END.

Databases v2 (today's default for named managed databases) has no node of its own: it is this node pointed at https://gateway.jelou.ai/datum-db/<slug>/api/..., authenticated with an x-api-key header. The DATUM node is Databases (Legacy) and is not the type to reach for on a new build.
Do not execute pre/post scripts during validation or compilation.
Preserve pre/post scripts as strings; workflow-core never executes them or makes a request.

settings.proxyOptions is optional in this revision. The engine's own Settings type declares it as required (http/types.ts:40), but the executed path destructures `requestSettings ?? {}` (utils/index.ts:120) and only touches the proxy behind `proxy?.enabled &&` (utils/index.ts:146); the executed path outranks the declared type.

Unsupported authentication types degrade instead of failing: the auth switch falls to default: break (utils/index.ts:219-220), the request is sent unauthenticated. This revision documents the degradation and does not turn it into a rejection.

The five-value method enum is a package narrowing: the engine passes the configured value straight through as an axios Method (utils/index.ts:161, 190) and no rejection of another verb was demonstrated.
The precedence between settings.timeout, settings.mtlsTimeout and the plan cap inside resolveRequestTimeout (utils/index.ts:186) was not characterized and is not stated by this contract.
Success and node errors are routed by the fixed node-type switch (workflow-engine.service.ts:1853-1869): an error response follows the failed edge instead of crashing the execution.

The router has no specific selection for this type: selectNodeTypeRouting returns every candidate edge through default: return { edges } (legacy-routing-selector.ts:131-153), so sourceHandle is ignored and all connected edges fan out in stored order.
Runtime resources, templates, and side effects are never resolved or executed by workflow-core.
Precondition: The endpoint and any credentials are authorized outside workflow-core.

rules: Never write a START node. The tool adds the workflow's one START (`validate --fix` and `jelou push` write it), unless the workflow enters only through a WEBHOOK.
Your first edge is { "sourceId": "START", "targetId": "<first-node>", "branch": "default" }. "START" is a reserved alias the tool resolves to the real START id; no other node may use that id.
The first node cannot be START, WEBHOOK, EMPTY, NOTE.
WEBHOOK is optional, at most one per workflow, and never chained to START.

A workflow or tool that enters only through a WEBHOOK needs no START: write no edge from "START" and the tool adds none. A channel message or a TOOL node never starts it then. A marketplace skill always needs START.
Next to a wired WEBHOOK that feeds the flow, a START with no edge is only a warning: the tool wires nothing to it and push keeps it.
